Standard: Exposure to rotational velocities and accelerations (externally-applied forces) for the stated life documented in engine tech data does not adversely affect the engine beyond the capability established in 7.2 standards, nor result in exceeding defined engine operating limits, detrimental permanent deformation, or damage when the engine is operated at maximum allowable steady-state engine speed throughout the engine operating envelope IAW 7.3.1. Two additional gyroscopic conditions are assessed. Defined accelerations and rates for these conditions are applied at, or about, the air vehicle CG; compatible engine loads are derived based on installed engine position in air vehicle: a. 1.4 rad/s about any axis in a plane perpendicular to the engine rotor axis combined with any LF conditions occurring within the flight envelope for 107 cycles. Engine structure does not exhibit detrimental permanent set, damage, or life reduction, or temporarily deflect to the extent that operation or performance is impaired. If this condition is tailored based on rational assessment of installed air vehicle characteristics and flight data then, at a minimum, rotor structure will still be evaluated for the 1.4 rad/s condition as stated to ensure HCF capability under maneuver conditions. b. 3.5 rad/s about any axis in a plane perpendicular to the engine rotor axis combined with a ±1g vertical maneuver load for a period of 15 seconds. Engine structure does not fail, there is no uncontained failure or fire, and the engine maintains performance enabling successful recovery of air vehicle. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Analyses are accomplished to verify strength, deflection, and fatigue capability, and system-level impacts.
